title: Naloxone Supply Under Australia's National Take-Home Naloxone Program During the Emergence of Nitazene-Related Harms
content: Introduction: Take-home naloxone is a key component of overdose prevention efforts in Australia. We examined national trends in naloxone supply under Australia's National Take-Home Naloxone (THN) Program, including exploring potential drivers for periods of increased naloxone supply. Methods: Monthly naloxone supply data were obtained for the period July 2022 to June 2025 and examined nationally and by jurisdiction. Interrupted time series analyses were undertaken to assess changes in pharmacy naloxone supply following key events. Level and slope changes were estimated using segmented regression models accounting for seasonality and autocorrelation. Results: Naloxone supply increased substantially over the study period, rising from 196,461 units in the first full year of the program to 343,643 units in the second year and 474,825 units in the third year. Growth was driven primarily by pharmacy distribution, with much smaller quantities supplied via hospitals and authorised suppliers such as needle and syringe programs. Victoria accounted for the largest proportion of naloxone supplied nationally. Two events associated with synthetic opioids were associated with significant increases in pharmacy naloxone supply. Discussion: Naloxone supply increased substantially during the first three years of Australia's National Take-Home Naloxone Program. The largest increases in pharmacy naloxone supply coincided with periods of heightened awareness of synthetic opioid harms. Continued monitoring of naloxone supply may help inform our understanding of how emerging drug threats and other events drive community uptake of THN.
